t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop website section, flat straight-on UI mockup on a deep navy background with a soft vignette. Top-left: a small mono section eyebrow, a large light-weight sans headline and a one-line limestone subhead. Centre: a fine 1.5 px off-white P&ID-style process schematic of tanks, filters and pipes, encircled by overlapping glowing orbit rings in cream and steel blue with luminous node dots. Thin leader lines run from the nodes to labels in two columns at the left and right edges showing <CONTENT> in monospace, each with a small outlined link button. Corner plus marks, faint frame lines, generous negative space. Calm, precise, technical.
signature_idea: The plant schematic sits at the centre of glowing orbits, and each standard is a planet-like node on a ring that points back to the part it governs.
strengths: one striking hero visual that is still made of brand-native line drawing
monospace standard codes read as precise and auditable
proof links under every label support the 'show the evidence' message
navy and limestone with steel-blue accent is close to palette
clear left/right label columns keep it scannable
weaknesses: orbits do not encode anything, so it fails the 'which standard governs each part' question it claims to answer
glow and bloom drift toward sci-fi cliché and away from calm print precision
schematic labels are tiny and illegible
many overlapping arcs add visual noise
brand_fit_why: Navy ground, fine line schematic, light Geist-like headline and mono codes are on-brand, but the glowing orbital sci-fi treatment is more theatrical than the calm, precise brand book wants.
